prompt:
Task: faithful HD remaster of a sheet of animation frames from the 1993 adventure game Sam & Max Hit the Road (LucasArts). This is a production asset. Every frame replaces one original frame in the game, at the same size and position, and the frames are played one after another.

Input: the attached image is the original low-resolution sheet enlarged exactly 4x with hard pixel edges. The frames stand apart on a plain flat magenta background (#FF00FF). Around the sheet is a plain gray (#808080) border. The background and the border are only padding.

What the sheet shows: Max, the white rabbit-like creature (long ears, wide toothy grin, no clothes). The description is only a help; the input image decides. On this sheet, row by row from left to right: start pose, facing right (7 frames). The game mirrors the frames facing right when the character faces left, so there are no frames facing left; do not add any.

Size rule (most important): draw every frame at exactly the size it has in the input, with the same height, the same width and the same proportions of head, body, arms, legs and props. One input pixel is 4 output pixels for every frame on this sheet and on every other sheet of this character, so the character never grows, shrinks or changes shape between frames. On this sheet the frames are from 40 to 148 pixels tall and from 68 to 248 pixels wide in the input (the box around each frame's visible pixels); jobb.json lists every frame's box under ruter (synlig, in original pixels: multiply by 4).

Do:
- Trace every frame at 4x in high resolution, so it looks like the characters of Day of the Tentacle Remastered next to their originals: keep the pose, silhouette and proportions, and turn every cluster of pixels into the shape it shows (glasses, a tie, a shoe). Clean dark anti-aliased outlines with a little variation in weight, flat colors with one shade and a few highlights, the same color for every area as in the input. No dithering, no texture, no gradients, no pixel steps.
- Keep the original design: the same character, the same colors, light direction, shadows and contrast as in the input.
- Make all frames look identical apart from the pose: the same face, eyes, hat, clothes, colors and light in every frame. Any difference between frames flickers in the game.
- Keep the pose and silhouette of every frame, and keep each frame in its place on the sheet, in the same rows and the same order.
- Glowing effects (light, lightning, sparks, fire) are painted as soft glow that fades into transparency.

Do not:
- Do not add, remove, merge, split or redesign frames.
- Do not add anything that is not in the input: no new props, accessories, patterns, logos, text, shadows, floor, numbers, labels, frames or grid lines.
- Do not change colors, clothes or proportions, and do not make heads, hands or eyes bigger than in the input.
- Some frames show only part of the character (a body without a head, a head alone, an arm), because the game draws the parts separately. Paint them as they are and do not complete them.
- Do not let frames touch or overlap each other.
- No photorealism, no modern 3D look, no film grain, no vignette, no watermark, no signature.

Output: one PNG image, exactly 1536 x 1024 pixels, with a fully transparent background (real alpha: no background color and no gray border) and every frame in the same place as in the input. Before delivering, run python3 verktoy/sjekk_leveranse.py jobber/fig017_02/resultat.png and redo the frames it reports as too big, too small, moved or missing. List the delivery with its sha256 in the fremdrift.json of your report and add a rutekart (the box around each frame's drawing, alpha above 128).

If a second image is attached, it is the approved master sheet (hovedark) of this character, or an already approved HD sheet of the same character, or an approved HD picture from the same game. Paint the character exactly as in that image: the same face, hair, clothes, colors and level of detail. Take every pose, size and position from the first image. If a third image is attached, it is the master sheet of the second character on the sheet.


SELECTED ATLAS PRODUCTION PASS. The text above is the preserved complete-sheet brief. For THIS call, Image 1 is a selected source atlas. Render exactly its separate complete source drawings, in the same cells, size and position, rather than generating the complete job sheets. Image 2 is Max's approved master, used only for identity and clean Purcell drawing style. Image 1 controls every pose, partial layer, proportion, shadow palette, internal hole, separate particle and visible detail. Do not copy a pose or bright color from the master onto a deliberately dark source. Output one 1536 x 1024 RGBA image on genuinely transparent background, no magenta, white, gray, checkerboard, labels, grid, ground shadow or glow. Clean smooth hand-drawn curves and flat original colors, no pixel steps, texture or extra details. Every selected source cell is a single complete painting even when it contains multiple characters or disconnected parts. Leave all unused space transparent and keep paintings inside their own cell with generous separation.

Verified game context: the opening laboratory, room 2, palette 0, primary script 65. Max first confronts the green laboratory antagonist in a stylized cartoon scuffle which becomes separate gray dust clumps. Later Max handles the small fictional orange/tan clockwork prop and goes toward the car. Preserve the literal source drawings and their sequence. Never restore hidden bodies or replace shadow colors with normal colors.

Cell 1: costume017_1955, rectangle [0, 0, 768, 512], drawing top-left [282, 196], visible size [204, 120]. Only the intentionally small dark silhouette or disconnected fragment shown as Max disappears behind the car. Preserve this exact black/gray shape and any tiny blue-gray or pale colored mark; no completed character, eyes or extra details. Keep the internal holes and separate dots exactly as shown.
